question: Who among the following attacked Gujarat and plundered the Somnath Temple in the 11th century?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Mahmud of Ghazni__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Somnath Temple** in **Gujarat** was attacked and plundered in the **11th century** by **Mahmud of Ghazni**.
 
• Specifically, this raid occurred in** 1025 **during one of **Mahmud's multiple invasions** of Indian kingdoms.
 
• His attack resulted in the destruction of the** jyotirlinga of the Somnath Temple**.
 
• This invasion is also known for the** punitive invasion of Anhilwara** that followed the **conquest of Somnath**.
 
• Notably, despite the destruction, there are records of **pilgrimages **to the temple in **1038** that do not mention damage, signifying potential repairs or rebuilds during this period.
 
• Indeed, the temple was later rebuilt, only to face destruction once again during **Alauddin Khalji's conquest of Gujarat**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ahmad Shah Abdali:**

 
 
• **​**Ahmad Shah Abdali also known as Ahmad Shah Durrani was imprisoned along with his brother Zulfikar in Shah Hussain Hotak's fortress in Old Kandahar in his early years.
 
• His numerous attacks led to the destruction of the Mughal Empire, creating a power vacuum.
 
• Abdali significantly impacted the northern Maratha's aspirations at Panipat through his consistent invasions, reflecting his tireless energy and ambition.
 
• His Afghan army emerged victorious from the battle after successfully destroying several Maratha flanks which led to a massive loss of between 60,000 and 70,000 troops.
 
 
 
• **Qutubuddin Aibak:**
 
 
• **​**Qutubuddin Aibak was the founder of the Ghulam Dynasty or Slave Dynasty in India, ruling from 1206 to 1210 AD.
 
• He started his career as a slave of Muhammad Ghori who later appointed him as the general.
 
• He is known for starting the construction of Qutub Minar, one of the historical monuments in Delhi, though it was completed by his successor, Iltutmish.
 
• Qutubuddin died in a polo accident in Lahore in 1210.
 
 
 
• **Mahmud of Ghazni:**
 
 
• ​Mahmud of Ghazni was a Persianate Muslim who invaded the Indian subcontinent 17 times, most notably in 1025 when he attacked and plundered the Somnath Temple in the 11th century.
 
• His invasion of Somnath resulted in the destruction of the Jyotirlinga of the temple.
 
• He was also known for his punitive invasion of Anhilwara that followed the conquest of Somnath.
 
• Despite the destruction, there are records of pilgrimages to the temple in 1038 that do not mention any damage, suggesting potential repairs or rebuilds during this period.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad Bin Qasim:**
 
 
• ​Muhammad Bin Qasim was an Umayyad general who, at the age of 17, began the first Muslim conquest of the Indian subcontinent in the 8th century.
 
• He conquered Sindh and Multan which became the easternmost province of the Umayyad Caliphate.
 
• Qasim is known for his fair administration, which provided a level of stability in the areas he conquered.
 
• He was recalled to Damascus after a political revolt and thereafter completely disappeared from historical records, with his ultimate fate uncertain.
